questions.question: Which is the first garden tomb in the Indian subcontinent?

options.text: Tomb of Salim Chishti in Fatehpur Sikri
Tomb of Hoshang Shah in Malwa

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun's Tomb in Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Humayun's Tomb** is recognized as the first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's first wife, **Bega Begum** (also known as Haji Begum) in 1569-70.
 
• The tomb was designed by Persian architect **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**.
 
• This architectural marvel is located in **Nizamuddin East, Delhi, India**.
 
• Humayun's Tomb served as an inspiration for several major architectural innovations, including the Taj Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Significance**

 
 
• Humayun's Tomb is a fine example of Mughal architecture, which combines Persian and Indian styles.
 
• The use of red sandstone and white marble was pioneering for Mughal structures.
 
• Its charbagh (four-quartered) garden layout became a blueprint for future Mughal gardens.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• The site was praised for its cultural significance and exemplary preservation of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **Restoration Efforts**
 
 
• The Aga Khan Trust for Culture has undertaken significant restoration work on the tomb and its gardens.
 
• Efforts have been made to restore the original water channels and pathways within the charbagh.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Later Structures**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb influenced the design of later Mughal structures, including the Taj Mahal.
 
• The tomb's double-dome structure and high arches became a staple in Mughal architecture.

questions.question: Barabar Caves are in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Barabar Caves **are located in the **Jehanabad **district of Bihar, India.
 
• These caves date back to the Maurya Empire during the reign of Emperor Ashoka (273–232 BCE).
 
• They are known for their **rock-cut architecture **and are some of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India.
 
• The caves are primarily associated with the Ajivika sect, an ancient Indian religious community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajivika Sect:**

 
 
• Ajivika was an ancient Indian heterodox sect that existed during the same period as Jainism and Buddhism.
 
• The sect believed in determinism and the concept of fate (Niyati).
 
 
 
• **Barabar Hill Caves:**
 
 
• The Barabar Hill Caves consist of four main caves: **Lomas Rishi Cave, Sudama Cave, Karan Chaupar Cave, and Visvakarma Cave**.
 
• The interiors of these caves have highly polished surfaces, which is a unique feature.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Emperor Ashoka was a ruler of the Maurya Dynasty and one of India's greatest emperors.
 
• He converted to Buddhism and played a key role in spreading Buddhism across Asia.

questions.question: ​Paintings of Lepakshi are found in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lepakshi temple is located in the Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• The temple is renowned for its exquisite murals and frescoes that date back to the Vijayanagara Empire of the 16th century.
 
• These paintings depict scenes from Hindu mythology, particularly the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The mural art in Lepakshi is known for its vibrant colors and intricate details, showcasing the artistic excellence of the Vijayanagara period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• An empire based in the Deccan Plateau region in South India, established in 1336.
 
• It is known for its patronage of art, architecture, and culture.
 
• The empire played a critical role in preventing the spread of Islam in South India.
 
 
 
• **Mural Art:**
 
 
• A painting applied directly to a wall, ceiling, or other large permanent surfaces.
 
• Mural art has been used to depict historical events, religious stories, and cultural motifs.
 
 
 
• **Frescoes:**
 
 
• A type of mural painting executed upon freshly laid lime plaster, allowing the paint to become an integral part of the wall surface.
 
• Frescoes are known for their longevity and vibrant colors.
 
 
 
• **Ramayana and Mahabharata:**
 
 
• Two major ancient Indian epics that hold significant cultural and religious importance in Hindu tradition.
 
• The Ramayana narrates the life of Prince Rama, while the Mahabharata details the Kurukshetra War and the fates of the Kaurava and the Pandava princes.

questions.question: The dance form Kuchipudi originated in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The dance form is named after the village of **Kuchipudi** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative/dramatic character.
 
• This dance form incorporates both **nritta (pure dance)** and **nritya (expressive dance)** elements.
 
• The dance traditionally tells stories from Hindu epics and mythology, especially those of Lord Krishna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology in Kuchipudi:**

 
 
• **Natya:** The dramatic element of dance, including the spoken word.
 
• **Nritta:** The pure dance movements performed rhythmically without any interpretative aspect.
 
• **Nritya:** The expressive aspect of dance that conveys a narrative or emotions.
 
• **Abhinaya:** The art of expression in Indian classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dance form was originally performed by male Brahmins known as **Bhagavathalu**.
 
• It evolved into a more inclusive art form over time, now performed by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Famous Practitioners:**
 
 
• Some renowned Kuchipudi dancers include **Yamini Krishnamurthy** and **Sobha Naidu**.
 
• These artists have significantly contributed to the propagation and modernization of Kuchipudi.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Music:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dancers wear traditional attire, which includes a saree for women and a dhoti for men, often adorned with jewelry.
 
• The music accompanying Kuchipudi is typically Carnatic, and performances often feature live musicians.

questions.question: In Dravidian architecture, 'Vritta' represents which shape of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**circular**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Dravidian architecture, 'Vritta' specifically denotes a **circular shape**.
 
• This term is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vritta', which means **circle** or round.
 
• The circular shape is often used in temple layouts, especially in designing certain sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha).
 
• Dravidian architecture is prominent in South India and includes famous examples like the Brihadeeswara Temple in Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture**

 
 
• It is characterized by pyramid-shaped temples (Vimana) and elaborate carvings.
 
• Major elements include Gopuram (gateway towers), Vimana (temple sanctum), and Mandapa (pillared halls).
 
• Prominent examples include Meenakshi Temple, Brihadeeswara Temple, and Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple.
 
 
 
• **Temple Layouts**
 
 
• Temples are often laid out in geometric patterns, including squares, rectangles, and circles.
 
• The layout is designed to follow the principles of Vastu Shastra, an ancient Indian science of architecture.
 
 
 
• **Vastu Shastra**
 
 
• An ancient Indian science that dictates architectural practices to harmonize with natural forces.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of directional alignments and spatial geometry.
 
 
 
• **Brihadeeswara Temple**
 
 
• Located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, and built by Raja Raja Chola I.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and a prime example of Dravidian architecture.
 
• The temple features intricate carvings and a massive Vimana.

questions.question: Which book is called the Encyclopedia of Indian Sculpture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayastambha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vijayastambha is often referred to as the Encyclopedia of Indian Sculpture due to its intricate and detailed carvings.
 
• It is also known as the Victory Tower and is located in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan.
 
• The tower was constructed by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khilji in 1448.
 
• The structure stands at a height of approximately 37.19 meters and consists of nine stories.
 
• The intricate carvings on the Vijayastambha depict various gods, goddesses, musical instruments, and weapons, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kiradu Temple**

 
 
• Located in Barmer, Rajasthan, the Kiradu Temples are a group of temples known for their intricate sculptures and architectural grandeur.
 
• The temples are predominantly dedicated to Lord Shiva and date back to the 11th century.
 
 
 
• **Ranakpur Temple**
 
 
• The Ranakpur Jain Temple is one of the largest and most important temples of Jain culture, situated in Rajasthan.
 
• It is renowned for its stunning marble architecture and is dedicated to Tirthankara Adinatha.
 
 
 
• **Delwara Temple**
 
 
• Located on Mount Abu in Rajasthan, the Delwara Temples are a group of Jain temples known for their exquisite marble carvings.
 
• These temples were built by Vimal Shah and designed by Vastupala Tejpal, a Jain minister.

questions.question: Which of the following states is known for Bihu music?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihu** is a set of three important Assamese festivals- **Bohag Bihu, Kati Bihu,** and **Magh Bihu**.
 
• **Bihu music** is an integral part of these festivals and is characterized by its **lively and rhythmic tunes**.
 
• It is associated with the traditional dance form called **Bihu dance**, which is performed by both young men and women.
 
• Bihu music typically features traditional instruments like the **Dhool (drum), Pepa (hornpipe), Toka (clapper), Gagana, and Baanhi (flute)**.
 
• The lyrics of Bihu songs generally reflect themes of **love, nature, and rural life in Assam**.
 
• Assam is located in the **northeastern region of India** and is known for its **rich cultural heritage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Punjab**__

 __
 
• Punjab is known for its vibrant and energetic **Bhangra** music and dance, which is very different from Bihu music.
 
• Bhangra is performed during the harvest festival of **Vaisakhi** and other celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan**__
 __
 
• Rajasthan is famous for its **folk music and dance forms** like **Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Kathputli**.
 
• The music often features instruments like the **Sarangi, Dholak, and Kartal**.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__
 
 
• Tamil Nadu is renowned for its **Carnatic music** and traditional dance form **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• Carnatic music is known for its complex **raga (melodic scales) and tala (rhythmic cycles)**.

questions.question: Quwwat-al-islam mosque is nearest to which of the following historical monuments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutub Minar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quwwat-al-Islam Mosque** is situated within the complex of the **Qutub Minar**.
 
• The mosque was built by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**, the founder of the Mamluk Dynasty in India.
 
• It is one of the earliest surviving mosques in India, dating back to the late **12th century**.
 
• The mosque is located in the **Qutub Complex** in Mehrauli, Delhi.
 
• The complex also includes other structures like the **Iron Pillar** and the **Alai Darwaza**.
 
• The Qutub Minar is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Humayun's Tomb**__

 __
 
• Humayun's Tomb is located in **Nizamuddin East, Delhi**.
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's wife, **Empress Bega Begum**, in the year **1569-70**.
 
• The tomb is a fine example of **Mughal architecture**.
 
• It is also a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
 
 
• **Tughlakabad Fort**__
 __
 
• Tughlakabad Fort is located in **Delhi**.
 
• It was built by **Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq**, the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, in the early **14th century**.
 
• The fort is a massive structure with strong fortifications.
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid**__
 
 
• Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India.
 
• It is located in **Old Delhi**.
 
• The mosque was commissioned by **Shah Jahan** in the year **1656**.
 
• It is also known as **Masjid-i Jahan-Numa**.

questions.question: 'Navroz' is celebrated as the new year by which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parsi:**

 
 
• Navroz, also known as Nowruz, is the Persian New Year, celebrated by the Parsi community, who are followers of Zoroastrianism.
 
• It marks the first day of spring and the renewal of nature.
 
• Parsis celebrate Navroz with traditional rituals, including prayers, feasts, and the setting of a special table called the Haft-sin.
 
• It is a time for family gatherings and the exchange of gifts.
 
• Navroz has pre-Islamic roots, and is a very old celebration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Christian:**

 
 
• Christians celebrate the New Year on January 1st, according to the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Different Christian denominations may have other significant dates related to religious observances, but January 1st is the widely recognized New Year's Day.
 
• Christian celebrations often include church services, family gatherings, and festive meals.
 
• The date of Easter is also a very important date for Christians.
 
• The celebration of christmas is also a major holiday.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist:**
 
 
• Buddhists observe various New Year celebrations depending on their cultural and regional traditions.
 
• In Theravada Buddhist countries like Thailand, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka, the New Year (Songkran) is typically celebrated in April.
 
• In Tibetan Buddhism, Losar is the New Year, which usually falls in February or March.
 
• Buddhist New Year celebrations often involve temple visits, prayers, and community festivities.
 
• Buddhist celebrations often reflect the local culture.
 
 
 
• **Sikh:**
 
 
• Sikhs celebrate Vaisakhi as their New Year, which usually falls on April 13th or 14th.
 
• Vaisakhi also commemorates the formation of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.
 
• Sikh celebrations include visits to gurdwaras, kirtan (devotional singing), and community gatherings.
 
• Vaisakhi is a very important religious holiday.
 
• The celebration is often a very festive occasion.
